title: Typed student records
description:
Describe students with types and let the compiler catch mistakes.

```
Ada (id 1): average 88.3, best subject maths
Bob (id 2): no grades yet
```
hints: After `const avg = average(s); if (avg === null) ...`, TypeScript knows `avg` is a `number` in the rest of the function (lesson 5.03).
requirements: `interface Student { id: number; name: string; grades: Record<string, number>; email?: string }`.
`average(s: Student): number | null` returns `null` when there are no grades.
`best(s: Student): string | null` is the subject with the highest grade.
`describe(s: Student): string` gives the line above; no `any` anywhere.
stretch: Add `type NewStudent = Omit<Student, "id">` and a function that gives a new student the next id.
